title: Continuous release choreography: deterministic descriptor generator + canary schedule
creator: Aarti Mehta
description: Goal: implement a deterministic release descriptor generator and an adaptive canary schedule as part of the model onboarding CD pipeline. This ticket wires together the artifact fingerprinting step, compact release descriptor creation, automated smoke and perf validation harness, and a canary fraction scheduler that promotes or retracts performance profiles based on measured regressions. The focus is operationalizing safe, auditable, and replayable profile promotions with clear rollback triggers and short mean-time-to-recovery for regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline emits a compact deterministic descriptor (SHA256 + semantic metadata) for every onboarded model artifact
Descriptor is recorded in the release ledger and includes pointers to the signed artifact, perf profile, and test snapshot
Canary scheduler accepts a schedule + failure thresholds and runs canary traffic in Dedicated and Hosted envs
Automated smoke + perf checks run in CI and gate profile promotion; regressions auto-mark a promote as failed
Rollback hook triggers a profile retraction and notifies stakeholders (Slack + email) within 5m of a failing canary
End-to-end test (ci/integration) covering descriptor generation -> canary -> promote -> rollback passes in CI every commit
ci_jobs: ci/onboard/descriptor-gen (runs on artifact build, writes descriptor to ledger)
ci/onboard/smoke-and-perf (executes smoke tests and a lightweight perf sample against canary)
ci/onboard/canary-schedule (deploys a canary, monitors thresholds, triggers promote/retract)
ci/integration/descriptor-replay-test (replays descriptor to verify idempotent promotion)
test_plan: Unit tests for descriptor schema + deterministic sorting of metadata fields
Integration test: push artifact -> descriptor emitted -> ledger entry created -> canary executed
Chaos test: inject latency/faults into canary target to verify rollback path and notifications
Performance regression test: synthetic workload validates compare-delta thresholds for every profile promotion
notes: Spike (2025-02-20): proved deterministic descriptor is stable across builders if we normalize byte order and remove build-timestamp metadata.
Decision: ledger will store descriptor + signed artifact digest instead of full artifact to reduce storage and preserve provenance.
Trade-off: more conservative canary windows increase time-to-promote but reduce false positives; default schedule set to 10% traffic for 30m.
Follow-up: add an operator endpoint to force-retract a profile if automated rollback misses a subtle regression.
